This is the author and operator guide for figures across the site. It
replaces two earlier Academy guides — the Gemini-era document-generation
guide and the previous version of this page — whose pipeline was retired by
[ADR-093](../adr/adr-093-image-generation-svg.qmd). If a workflow you
remember is not on this page, check that ADR before using it.

## The two figure classes

Every figure on the site is one of two classes, and the class decides the
entire workflow ([ADR-093](../adr/adr-093-image-generation-svg.qmd) +
[ADR-103](../adr/adr-103-generated-illustrative-raster.qmd)):

| Class | Naming | Source of truth | Renderer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Diagram** — schematics, flows, architecture figures | `<doc>-diagram-NN-<slug>` | A committed `.svg`, authored by Claude Code in the house style | `scripts/render_svg_images.py`, deterministically, in CI |
| **Image** — illustrative art (covers, concept openers) | `<doc>-image-NN-<slug>` | A committed `.png` / `.jpeg` produced by a generative raster model under ADR-103 constraints | None — the committed raster *is* the artifact |

The dividing line is text: **anything that carries labels, arrows, or
words is a diagram and must be SVG.** Vector text is always exactly what
the source says, which makes the generative-raster spelling-defect class
(the reason ADR-093 exists) structurally impossible.

## Diagrams (ADR-093)

**Author:** write a `.svg` against the house style in
[`src/uiao/canon/svg-style/`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/canon/svg-style)
— `STYLE.md` is the rulebook, `palette.json` the colors (navy `#0D1B2E`,
teal `#1E8C8C`, amber `#D4A017`, mid-blue `#2E75B6`, grey `#5A5A5A`, on a
**white background**), and `template-16x9.svg` / `template-1x1.svg` the
starting canvases. Commit the SVG next to the document that uses it.

**Render:** the committed SVG is the source of truth; the sibling `.png`
the document references is a **derived build artifact**. The site build
rasterizes every SVG before Quarto renders, so published pages always
carry fresh PNGs. For local authoring or DOCX preview:

```bash
python scripts/render_svg_images.py
```

The script walks committed `*.svg`, rasterizes each (prefers `cairosvg`,
falls back to Playwright/Chromium for `<foreignObject>` or web fonts), and
writes the standard sidecar with `generator: claude-svg-v1`. Freshness is
the SHA-256 of the LF-normalized SVG text, recorded as the sidecar
`prompt_sha256` — an unchanged SVG with an existing PNG is skipped, so
re-running is free.

**Do not commit the PNG.** The `block-tracked-build-artifacts` pre-commit
hook and the `derived-binary-gate` CI workflow reject any PNG whose
sibling SVG is tracked; the grandfathered exceptions live in
`scripts/svg-derived-png-allowlist.txt` and that list only shrinks.

**Update:** edit the SVG, re-render locally to review, commit the SVG
change only. The text in the diagram changes exactly and only as the
source changes — there is no regeneration lottery.

## Images (ADR-103)

Illustrative art — book covers, concept openers — may be produced by a
generative raster model, because it carries no text. The
[ADR-103](../adr/adr-103-generated-illustrative-raster.qmd)
constraints are the contract:

- **No baked text.** Labels belong in the caption or a rendered overlay,
  never in the pixels.
- White background; PNG or JPEG only; **≥ 2400 px** on the long edge;
  **≤ 1.5 MB**; 16:9 or 1:1.
- The file is committed (there is no source to re-derive it from), named
  `-image-NN-`, with its `.png.json` sidecar recording generator and
  provenance.

Diagrams never travel this route — a "quick generated schematic" is how
misspelled labels reach federal-grade deliverables.

## The provenance contract

Both classes ship the same three metadata layers, so a figure remains
self-describing even detached from the repo:

1. **Deterministic filename** — `<doc-slug>-<class>-NN-<slug>.<ext>`;
   given the document and figure number you can compute the path.
2. **Sidecar JSON** — a sibling `.png.json` carrying `generator`,
   `prompt_sha256` (SVG-text hash for diagrams; prompt hash for images),
   `sha256` of the on-disk bytes, `generated_at`, and dimensions.
3. **PNG `tEXt` chunks** — the same provenance embedded in the binary, so
   it survives being pasted into a deck or emailed.

Reusable, multi-document figures are additionally registered in the
canonical image registry
([`src/uiao/canon/image-registry.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/image-registry.yaml),
UIAO_202), which tracks status, usage sites, and supersession. Hash
disagreement between the registry and on-disk files surfaces as
`DRIFT-PROVENANCE` under the
[Drift Detection Standard](../docs/16_DriftDetectionStandard.qmd);
registry-shape violations surface as `DRIFT-SCHEMA`.

## Where documents come from (the surviving generation pipeline)

The retired guide also covered document assembly. What ships today:

- **The site** renders from `.qmd` via Quarto; every deploy also
  regenerates the per-section **DOCX bundles** (like this section's
  [academy-bundle.docx](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/download/downloads-latest/academy-bundle.docx)) and each page's individual
  DOCX download.
- **Figures reach DOCX/HTML the same way** — the rasterized PNG referenced
  by the page — so the SVG-first rule covers every output format.
- There is **no Gemini step anywhere**: no `GEMINI_API_KEY`, no
  prompts-to-raster generation for diagrams, no AI at render time. CI
  only rasterizes committed sources.

## Special-case tooling

- **orgpath-narrative illustrative images** use the fig-alt-as-prompt
  convention: the figure's `fig-alt` text is the generation brief, and
  `scripts/regenerate_local_images_from_figalt.py` materializes them.
  Audit coverage with `scripts/Invoke-OrgPathImageAudit.ps1`.
- **`scripts/generate_images.py`** survives only as a library — the
  renderer imports its sidecar/hash helpers — and as the legacy
  orchestrator behind `.github/workflows/image-gen.yml`. New figures do
  not start there.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Commit rejected: tracked build artifact | You staged a PNG whose sibling SVG is committed | Drop the PNG from the commit; the build renders it |
| Published figure is stale | The SVG changed but a stale committed PNG is allowlisted | Remove the pair from `svg-derived-png-allowlist.txt` and let CI render |
| Rasterized PNG missing a font or `<foreignObject>` content | `cairosvg` limitation | The renderer's Playwright fallback handles it; ensure Playwright/Chromium is installed locally |
| `DRIFT-PROVENANCE` on a registered figure | Prompt file, SVG, or PNG edited without updating the registry | Recompute via the renderer; land the registry update in the same PR |
| A diagram idea needs photographic texture | It's probably an *image*, not a diagram | Split it: raster art per ADR-103, with any labels in an SVG overlay or the caption |
